verdict.rationale: Cline's own docs say it can run long-running dev servers live, react to their output, use a browser, and take browser actions, which covers the core loop of observing a running web app from the assistant. There is no explicit documentation of debugging features such as reading console or network logs, inspecting the live DOM, or setting breakpoints, so depth is unproven. Missing for 10: documented live-app debugging (console/network/DOM inspection or debugger attachment), a detailed browser-tool workflow, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can debug a live running web application directly from my coding assistant

citations.quote: Executes in your terminal and reacts to output as it appears. Long-running dev servers, tests, deploys, all handled live.
It can read and write files, run terminal commands, use a browser, and help you build features through natural conversation.
Cline auto-approves everything: file changes, terminal commands, browser actions, MCP tools, and mode transitions.
Create files, run commands, browse the web, and use tools with human-in-the-loop approval.
